method: Fresh independent static audit of all 60 tooling_docs files from the frozen inventory. Read all production scripts, CI workflows, configuration, user/developer/acceptance documentation and license/notice text in full and judged their actual execution, failure, identity, privilege, selection, cleanup, evidence and documentation contracts. Read all nine tooling test files plus the native environment fixture in full, including their synthetic repositories and subprocess fixtures; additionally traversed their complete TypeScript ASTs and enumerated test registrations, assertions and branch structure using installed Rolldown parseSync without evaluating any test. Reviewed historical allowlist code as current policy only; no previous Git objects or audit conclusions were consulted. Read the entire lockfile structurally through a specialized indentation/section traversal, checking exact package.json/importer membership and versions, workspace override equality, all 336 integrity records and snapshots, and closure of all 623 dependency edges. Parsed and recursively traversed all 20 historical feature-evidence JSON files for schema, limits on their claims, source-reference and hash shape consistency; checked 178 unique method records and classification totals against the current 178 typed and 175 JSON protocol methods. Historical hash drift is retained as historical provenance, not used as current correctness evidence; historical passed assertions were not adopted or replayed. Checked all Markdown local link destinations for existence. Structural helper output is .work/public-https-round4-tooling-structure.json. Source snapshot checks before and after returned exactly 1880 files and the frozen digest. No tests, builds, package installations, network calls, old repository/history reads, credential access, or production changes occurred; only ignored audit artifacts were written. The separate ignored Linux execution-helper review is outside these 60 files and outside this source finding list. Static checks do not establish current external vulnerability status, upstream availability, real hosted CI or production integrations.
